- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast shows >10% spike from prior period, cap next period’s forecast at +5% of prior.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days below 65.00 after peak), model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns positive after day 15, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for final 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral), model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion correction to forecast.
